clue.text: Briefly go for and steal piece of cake

indicators.note: briefly means each of the two words is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to go for something is to pick it
to nick is to steal

explanation.surface: A greedy diner tells someone to grab a slice of cake and pinch it quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims both PICK and NICK, removing each final K.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is an idiom for a task that is very easy, just like a piece of cake.

clue.text: Really popular introduction to this bible book

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter, here of this

parts.note: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A popular preface to a scriptural book, praised as truly good.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is so in truth means it is actually or really so.

clue.text: Annoying people breaking ranks?

indicators.note: breaking the ranks scatters its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Troublemakers in the army who step out of line.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a nark is an irritating, grumbling person (also an informer).
explanation.definitionFit: A nark in British slang is an irritating or complaining person, so narks are annoying people.

clue.text: Tom perhaps is infected by suspect rash — must get purging

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, given as an example

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or unsound, so the letters of is and rash are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tomcat catches a dubious skin rash and needs a good clean-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'infected by' is only a link here: 'suspect' is what mixes the fodder, and 'Tom' is a male cat rather than a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the purging of emotions, or medically the purging of the bowels.

clue.text: Temper effect of note cutting motorway access

indicators.note: cutting means the note slices into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI
a gate gives access
ti (te) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone reduces the impact of a memo blocking the way onto a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; its digit 1 is read as the letter I. 'cutting' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To mitigate is to lessen or moderate how severe something is.

clue.text: Expert support — seamer keeps up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
the words support seamer keep the answer held inside them

explanation.surface: Cricket talk: a skilled helper, the seam bowler who keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards inside suppORT SEAMer: 'keeps' signals hiding and 'up' the reversal. A seamer is a cricket bowler who makes the ball move off its seam.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master or virtuoso, a highly skilled person.

clue.text: Fisherman may use this time on bitter lake

parts.note: a raw wind is a bitter one
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An angler spends time beside a lake in the bitter cold.
explanation.definitionFit: A trawl is a large fishing net dragged behind a boat.

clue.text: Jolt as vehicle is caught in high wind

indicators.note: being caught in a gale places the vehicle and is inside it

parts.note: a gale is a high wind
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van is buffeted by a strong wind, giving it a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise someone is to shock or jolt them into action.

clue.text: Extra digit written outside box

indicators.note: one word is written around the outside of the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a toe is a digit of the foot
to spar is to box

explanation.surface: An additional figure is scrawled on the outside of a carton.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to spare is left over, surplus or extra.

clue.text: Spinners must accept most of those people bring about complete reversal

indicators.note: accepting means the shortened word is taken into the middle

parts.note: turntables are things that spin

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: them means those people

explanation.surface: Bowlers turning the ball must accept most players will produce a total turnaround.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinners' suggests cricket bowlers but means record decks.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tables is an idiom for reversing a situation so the disadvantaged side gains the upper hand.

clue.text: Fox hurt by youth lacking boundaries

indicators.note: without its boundaries the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: to smart is to hurt or sting

explanation.surface: A fox is injured by a young lad behaving without limits.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle or outwit them.

clue.text: Source of anxiety in retreating tiny animals

indicators.note: in places the first letter inside the reversed word
retreating means going backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: tiny means small

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Timid little creatures backing away in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American pack animals related to camels.

clue.text: Surrounded by cries of excitement, left car

indicators.note: being surrounded by puts the letter for left inside the cries

parts.note: whee is a cry of excitement

explanation.surface: Amid shrieks of joy, someone abandoned their vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheels is slang for a car or other vehicle.

clue.text: English public house on green mostly short-lived

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: emerald is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A traditional English pub on a village green that hardly lasts.
explanation.walkthrough: A village green is the shared grassy area in an English village, often beside the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means lasting for only a very brief time.

clue.text: Got excited at one bid

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An auction-goer becomes thrilled after a single offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have obtained something is to have acquired or got it.

clue.text: Precedents established in international trials?

definitions.meaning: legal cases whose outcome sets a precedent

explanation.surface: Legal rulings set in cross-border court hearings.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a lawsuit whose verdict serves as a precedent for later rulings.

clue.text: Stress rate applied to English unchanged

parts.note: mph (miles per hour) is a rate of speed
as is means left unchanged

explanation.surface: A tax rate on English goods stays the same, causing strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the stress or prominence placed on something.

clue.text: Rigid shaft under car must be cooler

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the bar comes below the car

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British car
a bar is a rigid shaft

explanation.surface: A stiff rod beneath a vehicle must be there to cool it.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibar is a small refrigerator in a hotel room, a cooler for drinks.

clue.text: Develops odds on heavy defeats

parts.note: SP is starting price, the betting odds at the start of a race
routs are heavy defeats

explanation.surface: A betting tale: odds placed on crushing losses grow.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the British bookmakers' term for the odds at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout is to grow or develop, as shoots do.

clue.text: The rest of the day?

parts.note: seems to mean the remaining hours, but means a rest taken during the day

explanation.surface: Asking about the remainder of today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' reads as remainder but means a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon nap, a rest taken in the middle of the day.

clue.text: 1000kg gold car cover

parts.note: a tonne is 1000 kilograms
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A tonne of gold kept under a tarpaulin on a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonneau is a detachable cover over the passenger area of an open car.

clue.text: Secret bankers backing number protecting me

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around the word me
backing means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a song is a musical number

explanation.surface: Clandestine financiers supporting a song that shields the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The gnomes of Zurich' is a nickname for shadowy Swiss bankers.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomes is a nickname for secretive international financiers, from the gnomes of Zurich.

clue.text: Harsh way to make money, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the letters are said aloud and match another word's sound

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way; to earn is to make money

explanation.surface: A severe method of making cash, according to rumour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict and severe in manner.

clue.text: Troubles in court shifted rioters at last

indicators.note: shifted letters are moved around into a new order
at last picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Rioters finally moved through the courts after unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ructions are noisy disturbances or troubles.

clue.text: Temper of Jack, leaving hurt

indicators.note: leaving means the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: to injure is to hurt
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: Jack's bad mood as he walks away injured.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to harden or toughen someone, as steel is tempered.

clue.text: Poor Rebecca's beau keeps uniform for dressing

indicators.note: keeps means the scrambled letters hold the extra one inside
poor means badly formed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Rebecca's unfortunate boyfriend wears a uniform when getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbecue sauce is a condiment or dressing for grilled food.

clue.text: Extends projections to include 50 per cent of loss

indicators.note: to include means the other letters go inside

parts.note: prongs are projecting points

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half of the word, its first two letters

explanation.surface: Financial forecasts are stretched to cover half the losses.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong something is to lengthen it in time.

clue.text: Increase rate of backing favourites and ahead

indicators.note: backing means the word is reversed

parts.note: pets are favourites
up means ahead, as in a team being up

explanation.surface: A punter raises stakes on favourites who lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To step up something is to speed it up or intensify it.
